text:
kevin: Heads-up — we had a noisy Xid on a p4 node in us-west-2a, and current evidence collection is inconsistent. can we agree on a tiny, reliable snapshot we can grab from nodes for fast attribution?

maria: yes — we need something that can be run by oncall (or an automated hook) and uploaded to S3 with tags. quick, minimal, and normalized. :thumbsup:

jas: agree. current trouble: dmesg lines vary between kernels, journalctl formats differ across distros, and nvidia-smi CSV output is all over the place. often we miss the nvml state.

kevin: proposal: a 6-file bundle (text-only) + metadata.json with clear keys. keep size < 100KB typical. files: 1) dmesg-tail.txt (recent kernel/GPU msgs) 2) journalctl-gpu.txt (journalctl -k/--dmesg filtered) 3) nvidia-smi-state.txt (nvidia-smi full -q) 4) nvidia-smi-processes.txt (nvidia-smi pmon or --query) 5) syslog-snippet.txt (if present) 6) gpu-kernel-modules.txt (lsmod | grep nvidia) + metadata.json referencing node, kernel, driver.

infra-bot: automated collection checklist:
- sample window: last 10m by default, fallback to last 200 dmesg lines
- enforce timezone=UTC in logs
- include kernel version and driver version in metadata

oncall: +1. can we standardize the dmesg command so timestamps and truncation are deterministic?

sam: put this in a small script that ships only matching lines and context. sample script:

```
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
OUTDIR="$1"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"
# kernel messages around nv
dmesg -T | grep -iE "(NVRM|Xid|Ecc|NVRM:|GPU|nv\b)" -n --context=5 | tail -n 500 > "$OUTDIR/dmesg-tail.txt" || true
# journalctl kernel + nvidia unit
journalctl -k -o short-iso --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -iE "(NVRM|Xid|ECC|GPU|nvidia)" > "$OUTDIR/journalctl-gpu.txt" || true
# full nvml snapshot
nvidia-smi -q > "$OUTDIR/nvidia-smi-state.txt" || true
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv,noheader > "$OUTDIR/nvidia-smi-processes.txt" || true
lsmod | grep -i nvidia > "$OUTDIR/gpu-kernel-modules.txt" || true
uname -a > "$OUTDIR/kernel-info.txt"
cat > "$OUTDIR/metadata.json" <<EOF
{\n  \"node\": \"$(hostname -s)\",\n  \"ts\": \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\",\n  \"kernel\": \"$(uname -r)\",\n  \"driver\": \"$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | head -n1 || echo unknown)\"\n}
EOF
```

jas: love it. two asks: 1) nvidia health counters (if available) e.g., `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ENCODER` 2) a small deterministic envelope file (single-line JSON) for indexing.

kevin: for the envelope, use one-line JSON with keys node, ts, gpu_id, xid_codes (list), short_message (first 140 chars of dmesg around hits). example: `{"node":"gpu-12","ts":"...","gpu_id":"0","xid_codes":[32],"short":"NVRM: Xid 31 at ..."}`

infra-bot: note: Xid mapping is noisy across driver versions. we should store raw Xid + driver version; for triage we can map common ones: 31=memory access, 43=ECC recovery? (approx). do not rely on mapping for automated drains.

oncall: what about retention and cost? we can't keep full bundles forever for 10k nodes. recommendation: keep envelope + 7d full bundles, 30d metadata index, S3 lifecycle to archive beyond.

sam: also add a small hashed id for correlating with pod/container stack: `cat /proc/1/cgroup` or `kubectl` context info if present. put in metadata.

alan: ops questions: when should we auto-drain node? if Xid repeated 3x in 1h across different processes + ECC warnings + driver version unchanged -> mark for drain. but we must avoid false positives from noisy workloads.

maria: add a quick heuristic in the oncall script that returns a triage score and reasons. score factors: xid_count, repeated_gpu_reset, ECC_count, mem_errors. output in metadata so SRE can decide.

jas: also log `dmesg -x` (extended flags) when available so offsets/encoded info stays consistent between kernels. and include a tiny parser snippet to extract numeric Xid codes and NVML error strings.

kevin: final action items: 1) sam to land the script as `/usr/local/bin/gpu-snapshot` with 0.1 safe defaults. 2) infra to add CI lint to validate metadata.json and envelope schema. 3) ops to define drain policy based on triage score and a manual override label.

oncall: I'll run the script on the affected node and upload bundle, ping back link. thanks all. :rocket:

infra-bot: template for S3 path: `s3://redwood-gpu-evidence/{region}/{node}/{ts}-{shortid}.tar.gz` and put tags: environment, driver, kernel, triage_score.

sam: I'll PR the script + small parser and add unit tests for the envelope normalization.

maria: nice, this should shave minutes off initial attribution. please include examples in runbook.

kevin: perfect. once PR merges, we'll wire a deploy hook that runs on early Xid detections and posts envelope to #incidents.

oncall: upload done: s3://redwood-gpu-evidence/us-west-2/gpu-22/1902468000-qp9.tar.gz — link posted to incident.

kevin: thanks — will follow up with a short postmortem after we see if drain was necessary.
